summary: Hosted API: elevated tail latency due to cache-bypass regression on embeddings route
description:
Deployment mode: Hosted API.

Issue summary:
Customer reports embeddings requests slowing down significantly starting ~11:30 UTC; p95 increased from ~450ms to 2.8s with occasional 10s outliers. No elevated 5xx, but they hit client-side timeouts.

Impact:
- Tail latency regression on /v1/embeddings
- Customer reported downstream batch jobs falling behind

Investigation notes:
- Observability shows cache hit-rate dropped from ~62% to ~4%
- Correlates with config push that changed request normalization for cache keys
- Regression appears limited to us-east edge.
comments: 2026-02-23 11:58 UTC (Chloe Martin): Confirmed latency spike and cache hit-rate drop on embeddings route. Escalating to runtime oncall.
2026-02-23 12:20 UTC (Rohan Mehta): Found config change: whitespace normalization toggled for embeddings input; cache keys no longer match prior entries.
2026-02-23 12:33 UTC (Rohan Mehta): Rolled back normalization change in us-east and re-warmed cache.
2026-02-23 13:05 UTC (Chloe Martin): p95 back to ~520ms. Customer confirms batch job recovering.
2026-02-24 09:10 UTC (Rohan Mehta): PR 9362 adds guardrails: require staged cache-key change + dashboard alert for sudden hit-rate drops.
2026-02-24 17:25 UTC (Chloe Martin): Closing ticket; RCA shared with customer.
resolution: Rolled back cache-key normalization change for embeddings and added guardrails/alerts to prevent cache-bypass regressions.
workaround: Customers with tight timeouts can temporarily increase embeddings timeout or batch size during cache re-warm; Support can route embeddings to alternate region if needed.
root_cause: Config change altered cache-key normalization, invalidating cache entries and forcing recomputation, leading to tail latency increase.
follow_ups: Add canary that checks cache hit-rate after config pushes
